1.
Rejoinder affidavit filed today is taken on record.

2. Heard Mr. Dinesh Kumar Chaudhary, learned counsel for the accused-applicant, as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Balgar for grant of bail, in Case Crime No.052 of 2022, under Sections 376-D, 365 and 370 IPC, lodged at Police Station Harraiya,
District Balrampur, during trial.
4. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.

In fact, the applicant and the victim were having a long-standing relationship and, they were frequently meeting and talking to each other and, the victim herself had left her home and arrived at the room of the applicant situated in Mumbai and, she, with her free wish and will, had Balgar vs State Of U.P. 1 solemnized marriage with the applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant has drawn attention of this Court towards Annexure-7, which is a declaration of marriage allegedly executed on 29.11.2021 by the applicant and victim.

It is vehemently submitted that the FIR against the applicant and his relatives has been lodged by the prosecutrix by stating wrong, concocted and false facts and the story, as cooked up by the prosecutrix, is highly improbable and could not be believed, moreover,
the incident is shown to have occurred on 24.11.2021 while the information to Superintendent of Police has been given on 31.01.2022 with the delay of more than two months and, since the application under Section 156(3) CrPC, on the basis of which FIR has been lodged, has been drafted by a legal professional, the allegations therein have been manipulated and exaggerated.

5. It is further submitted that there is material contradictions in the statement of the victim,
recorded under Sections 161 and 164 CrPC viz-a-viz the contents of the FIR and, the allegations, as levelled in her statements, are not finding corroboration with the medical evidence and, even if the prosecution version and her statements are believed on their face, the same may not travel beyond Section 498 IPC.
It is also submitted that the applicant has been languishing in jail in this case since 10.05.2022 and, he is not having any previous criminal history.
Charge sheet in this case has already been filed and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
6. Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that the victim/informant of the instant case was aged about 30 years on the date and time of the alleged incident and, she was a married lady and, the FIR of this case has been lodged by moving an application under Section 156 (3) CrPC, under the orders of a Magistrate.
No abnormality has been found in the medical examination report of the victim.

Various submissions have been advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant in order to show that the story, as cooked up by the victim in her FIR and statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 CrPC, could not be believed on their face in view of statement of husband of the victim as well as observations of the investigating officer whereby it is reflected that the applicant was regularly talking with the prosecutrix/victim in order to show that the victim, despite being a married to some other person, was having affair with the applicant and has herself gone to Mumbai in order to reside there with the applicant.
The applicant is in jail in this case since 10.05.2022 without any previous criminal antecedents.
Charge sheet in this case has also been filed and the presence of the applicant may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

8. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

9. Let the accused/applicant- Balgar involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court Balgar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178992988/

sentences.text: 2 concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
11. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

12. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
.
[Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.]
